## ShadowLLM: Overview

ShadowLLM was published at the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing in Miami, Florida.

## Key Contribution

ShadowLLM is a novel predictor that can shadow the LLM behavior and enforce better sparsity patterns, resulting in over 15% improvement in end-to-end accuracy compared to prior methods. ShadowLLM achieves up to a 20% speed-up over the state-of-the-art DejaVu framework.

## Overview

MaskLLM is a learnable pruning method that establishes Semi-structured (or "N:M") Sparsity in LLMs, aimed at reducing computational overhead during inference. The paper was presented as a NeurIPS 2024 Spotlight by researchers from NVIDIA and the National University of Singapore.

## Key Technical Approach

Instead of developing a new importance criterion, MaskLLM explicitly models N:M patterns as a learnable distribution through Gumbel Softmax sampling. This approach addresses a key challenge: the non-differentiability of mask selection and combination hinders the direct use of backpropagation for mask learning. The method incorporates Gumbel Softmax for differentiable sampling, which re-parameterizes the randomness of sampling into an independent random variable, making the probabilities of each mask candidate optimizable with gradient descent.

## Advantages

The approach offers two notable advantages: 1) High-quality Masks - the method effectively scales to large datasets and learns accurate masks; 2) Transferability - the probabilistic modeling of mask distribution enables the transfer learning of sparsity across domains or tasks.

## Performance

MaskLLM was assessed using 2:4 sparsity on various LLMs, including LLaMA-2, Nemotron-4, and GPT-3, with sizes ranging from 843M to 15B parameters, achieving a significantly lower 6.72 PPL on Wikitext compared to leading approaches that achieve a perplexity of 10 or greater.

The GPT-3 models tested utilize the standard transformer architecture with layer normalization, SwiGLU activation function, and Rotary Positional Embeddings (ROPE).

## La RoSA: Enhancing LLM Efficiency via Layerwise Rotated Sparse Activation

La RoSA (Layerwise Rotated Sparse Activation) is a novel method for activation sparsification designed to improve LLM efficiency without requiring additional training or magnitude-based pruning.

### Key Approach

The method leverages layerwise orthogonal rotations to transform input activations into rotated forms that are more suitable for sparsification, and by employing a Top-K selection approach within the rotated activations, achieves consistent model-level sparsity and reliable wall-clock time speed-up.

### Performance Results

For LLaMA2-7B at 40% sparsity, LaRoSA achieves a mere 0.17 perplexity gap with a consistent 1.30× wall-clock time speed-up, and reduces the accuracy gap in zero-shot tasks compared to the dense model to just 0.54%, while surpassing TEAL by 1.77% and CATS by 17.14%.

### Effectiveness and Scope

LaRoSA is effective across various sizes and types of LLMs, demonstrating minimal performance degradation and robust inference acceleration.

The paper was presented as a poster at ICML 2025 and addresses limitations of existing methods that either require time-consuming retraining or rely on unstable magnitude-based pruning approaches.

## SVD Contextual Sparsity Predictors for Fast LLM Inference

A framework provides a fast, training-free method for building sparse pattern predictors using truncation-aware singular value decomposition (SVD) of the gate projection matrix, along with a threshold calibration algorithm, and inference executors supporting conditional computation on CUDA and CANN devices.

### ReLUfication and Sparsity

ReLU activations naturally induce sparse activations, unlike smoother functions such as Swish or SiLU used in modern LLMs, and recent studies show that replacing them with ReLU variants plus fine-tuning recovers substantial sparsity. "ReLUfication" involves using fine-tuning to reintroduce ReLU-based activations and improve sparsity.

### Performance Results

Experiments on three sparse LLMs with an average activation sparsity level of 90% in the FFNs demonstrate up to a 1.8x reduction in end-to-end decoding time while maintaining less than 1% degradation in benchmark scores on tasks involving complex math and code generation.

### Technical Approach

Unlike existing contextual sparsity prediction methods, this approach provides theoretical guarantees regarding prediction accuracy. SVD predictors directly leverage the LLM's internal weight structure, avoiding out-of-distribution sensitivity issues that trained predictors face.

This research was published in March 2026 and represents recent advances in efficient LLM inference through sparsity-aware techniques.

## Overview

Polar Sparsity refers to the shift in sparsity importance from MLP layers to Attention layers as batch size and sequence length increase.

## Batch Size and MLP Neuron Sparsity

Under batching, we compute the union of active neurons across all sequences in the batch. Union neuron sparsity in MLP layers decreases rapidly with batch size, illustrating why MLP sparsity is less effective at scale. More specifically, SB typically grows, reducing the overall sparsity and limiting computational savings.

## Union Tokens

A neuron is retained if it is activated for any sequence in the current batch. Let SB ⊆[D] denote this union set for batch size B.

## Key Technical Approach

To efficiently compute sparse MLP activations, we design a custom GPU kernel that fuses indexing and matrix multiplication. Our kernel supports batched GEMM workloads and achieves near-linear speedups with increasing sparsity, with improvements of up to 5.5× over the dense baseline.

## Results

As batch size and sequence length grow, the importance of sparsity transitions from MLP layers, where union activation increases, to Attention layers, where head-level sparsity remains stable and batch-invariant. This delivers up to 2.2× end-to-end speedups in large-scale settings.

content.content:
# MaskLLM: Key Technical Details

## 1. Knowledge Distillation
**No KL divergence distillation is used.** MaskLLM optimizes frozen LLM weights directly against the language modeling loss: "all parameter blocks {𝒲i} are associated with the corresponding distributions {pπ(ℳi)}, and optimal distribution can be learned in an end-to-end manner" without a dense model teacher signal.

## 2. Training Cost
**Varies by model size:**
- LLaMA-2 7B: 1,280 GPU hours
- LLaMA-2 13B: 2,304 GPU hours  
- Nemotron-4 15B: 2,304 GPU hours
- Training uses 64 A100 GPUs with 8-way tensor parallelism for 2,000 steps

## 3. Sparsity Pattern
**Static, not input-dependent.** Each parameter block receives "the selection of corresponding masks {ℳi}" that are fixed post-training. The masks are determined via argmax over learned logits and applied uniformly across all inputs.

## 4. Gumbel Approach Difference
MaskLLM uses **Gumbel Softmax** (soft relaxation via softmax), not Gumbel-sigmoid. It produces "a soft and differentiable index" through: "y~i = exp((log(pi)+gi)/τ) / Σ exp((log(pj)+gj)/τ)" enabling gradient flow to probability distributions.

## 5. Sparsity Ratio & Models Tested
**2:4 sparsity** (50% parameter reduction) on:
- LLaMA-2 (7B, 13B)
- Nemotron-4 (15B)
- GPT-3 (843M, 2B)
- LLaMA-3 (8B)

**Achieved PPL improvements:** LLaMA-2 7B achieves 6.72 PPL versus SparseGPT's 10.42 on Wikitext-2.

A clustering-based activation pattern compression framework groups similar activation patterns into a small set of representative clusters. ## Overview

SDMPrune is a 2025 method titled "Self-Distillation MLP Pruning for Efficient Large Language Models" by authors Hourun Zhu and Chengchao Shen.

## Key Innovation

The method introduces a self-distillation loss during the pruning phase (rather than post-training) to fully exploit the predictions of the original model, thereby obtaining more accurate gradient information for pruning.

## Technical Approach

The researchers found that compared to attention modules, LLM predictions are less sensitive to multilayer perceptron (MLP) modules, which take up more than 5× parameters (in LLaMA3.2-1.2B), so they focus on the pruning of MLP modules to significantly compress LLMs without obvious performance degradation.

## Results

Experimental results on extensive zero-shot benchmarks demonstrate that the method significantly outperforms existing pruning methods. When applied with a 20% pruning ratio followed by finetuning, the SDMPrune-pruned model achieves competitive performance after just three epochs of finetuning, with only a marginal performance degradation of 0.1% compared to the original model.

## Availability

## Overview

WiSparse (Weight-aware Mixed-Granularity Training-free Activation Sparsity) leverages both activation and weight information for adaptive sparsity allocation.

## Key Innovation

The method identifies two key phenomena in modern LLMs: 1) less significant activations may align with highly important weights, and 2) sparsity sensitivity varies non-monotonically across model blocks.

## Methodology

WiSparse introduces a weight-aware mechanism integrating activation magnitudes with precomputed weight norms to accurately identify salient channels, combined with a mixed-granularity allocation scheme where a global budget is distributed across blocks via evolutionary search to protect sensitive regions, then refined within blocks to minimize reconstruction error.

## Performance Results

At 50% sparsity, WiSparse preserves 97% of Llama3.1's dense performance, surpassing the strongest baseline by 2.23 percentage points while achieving a 21.4% acceleration in end-to-end inference speed.

At a 30% sparsity level, performance degradation is negligible, with an average accuracy drop of just 0.22 percentage points across all models.

## Publication

## PATCH: Learnable Tile-level Hybrid Sparsity for LLMs

PATCH is a hybrid sparsity framework that enables a continuous sparsity ratio between 0% and 50%, partitioning weight matrices into tiles and assigning each tile to be either dense or 2:4 sparse via a learnable mask selection mechanism.

### Problem Statement

Existing approaches face challenges: unstructured sparsity preserves accuracy but yields irregular access patterns that prevent GPU acceleration, while semi-structured 2:4 sparsity is hardware-friendly but enforces a rigid 50% pattern that degrades model quality.

### Key Features

The design provides fine-grained control over accuracy-acceleration tradeoffs and supports non-uniform sparsity across layers, leading to superior overall quality. PATCH is compatible with tile-level sparsity acceleration libraries and compilers such as STOICC, making it the first hybrid sparsity method to demonstrate practical speedups.

### Performance Results

On LLaMA-2 7B with an A6000 GPU, PATCH achieves 1.18x-1.38x end-to-end speedup over dense baselines while improving accuracy by 0.37%-2.96% compared to the state-of-the-art 2:4 pruning method, MaskLLM.

### Implementation Variants

By jointly optimizing the sparsity within 2:4 tiles and the tile-level patterns during training, PATCH achieves higher accuracy than uniform sparsity across layers, and also offers a variant that tunes only the dense tiles while freezing the initial 2:4 mask for resource-constrained settings.

## WINA Overview

WINA (Weight Informed Neuron Activation) is a novel, simple, and training-free sparse activation framework that jointly considers hidden state magnitudes and the column-wise ℓ2-norms of weight matrices.

## Key Features

**Purpose and Benefits:**
The growing computational demands of large language models (LLMs) make efficient inference and activation strategies increasingly critical, and training-free sparse activation methods offer broader applicability and superior resource efficiency through their plug-and-play design.

**Addresses Prior Limitations:**
Many existing methods rely solely on hidden state magnitudes to determine activation, resulting in high approximation errors and suboptimal inference accuracy. WINA leads to a sparsification strategy that obtains optimal approximation error bounds with theoretical guarantees tighter than existing techniques.

## Experimental Results

WINA outperforms state-of-the-art methods (e.g., TEAL) by up to 2.94% in average performance at the same sparsity levels, across a diverse set of LLM architectures and datasets.

WINA reduces the overall (G)FLOPs by up to 60.0% on Qwen-2.5-7B, 63.7% on Llama-2-7B, 60.4% on Llama-3-8B, and 62.7% on Phi-4-14B at the 65% sparsity level.

## Implementation

This repository is the PyTorch implementation of WINA, a novel, simple, and training-free sparse activation framework that jointly considers hidden state magnitudes and the column-wise ℓ2-norms of weight matrices. The source code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/wina.

Beyond those, there are several critical recent competitors I'm finding: WAS is a training-free weight-aware activation sparsity method hitting 60% model-level sparsity, WINA from Microsoft (ICLR 2026) is training-free with 65% sparsity and outperforms TEAL by 2.94%, and WiSparse is another recent arXiv paper I need to examine further.

I'm also seeing a bunch of other approaches—SVD-based contextual sparsity predictors that achieve 90% sparsity but only work on ReLUfied models, SDMPrune using self-distillation for static structural pruning, and PATCH which uses learnable tile-level hybrid sparsity. There's also MGLU which is more of an architectural change rather than activation sparsity, and SparseInfer for training-free prediction.

Now I'm hitting a critical issue with the sparsity target—the original idea claimed 60% but I need to reconcile this against what these competitors are actually achieving.

The real problem is that training-free methods like WAS and WINA are already hitting 60-65% sparsity without any training cost, which completely undermines the value proposition of paying for a distillation-based predictor. And there's another fundamental limitation: batch size degrades MLP neuron sparsity rapidly because you're taking the union of active neurons across the batch, so focusing exclusively on MLP sparsity only works at batch_size=1. Plus, predictor overhead from approaches like DejaVu adds non-trivial latency that needs to be accounted for.

There are also existing open-source implementations from TEAL, R-Sparse, La RoSA, and WINA with Triton kernels that could be reused, and MaskLLM already covers similar ground with learnable Gumbel-based masks on SwiGLU models, though it targets static N:M sparsity rather than dynamic contextual sparsity. The core issue is becoming clearer: the fundamental premise of the approach has serious competitive and technical limitations that go beyond what was initially flagged.

The 60-70% sparsity target isn't actually novel since WAS and WINA already achieve 60-65% sparsity without any training, which undermines the claimed advantage of using distillation to reach higher sparsity levels. The "first predictor for SwiGLU" claim also doesn't hold up—ShadowLLM may have already evaluated on Llama-2, and multiple training-free methods now work on SwiGLU with comparable results. There's also a fundamental scalability problem: any method focusing on per-token MLP sparsity loses effectiveness as batch size increases. Most critically, if WINA achieves 65% sparsity with just a weight-norm lookup and zero predictor overhead, then adding a 15M-parameter predictor per layer becomes hard to justify unless it can significantly outperform that baseline.

This points toward needing a major rethinking rather than incremental fixes. The core problem—efficient decoding for SwiGLU models—is still worth solving, but the current approach needs fundamental changes. Where distillation-based predictors might still have an edge is in achieving better sparsity-accuracy tradeoffs: training-free methods might hit 60-65% sparsity but suffer quality degradation, whereas a learned predictor could potentially maintain output quality at higher sparsity levels like 65-75% by explicitly optimizing for distribution matching. Another angle is adaptive sparsity allocation—instead of fixed heuristics like magnitude or weight norms, a learned predictor could discover non-obvious patterns that better preserve model quality. There's also potential in integrating this with other compression techniques like simultaneous quantization and sparsity.

But the bar is much higher now.
